instagram.caption:
Contractor close rate: how to work out yours. For roofing, plumbing and HVAC business owners.
ServiceTitan data on its own customer accounts (May to Jul 2026): regional median close rates ran from 31% in the Northeast to 38% in the West. Among the top 25% of shops by close rate in each region, medians ran 70% to 73%.

Numbers Clinic, Lesson 8: the math.
Close rate = jobs sold / estimates given, both counted over the same month.
Example: 40 estimates, 14 sold. 14 / 40 = 35%.
Every Friday, write down two numbers: estimates given and jobs sold.
Then run it in dollars: $ sold / $ quoted. If the dollar rate is lower, your bigger quotes are the ones getting away.

The catch: ServiceTitan's page doesn't define close rate, and it says the data isn't representative of the whole trades industry. So the first number to beat is your own, from last month.

Send this to whoever writes your estimates.

youtube.title: Contractor Close Rate: How to Work Out Yours (Roofing, Plumbing, HVAC)
youtube.description:
Contractor close rate: how to work out yours, for roofing, plumbing and HVAC business owners.
For home service business owners who give estimates.
ServiceTitan, "Trades Industry Trends: Call Booking, Close Rates & Off-Hours Calls" (Oct 22, 2026): based on an aggregated, de-identified sample of ServiceTitan customer accounts, regional median close rates ranged from 31% in the Northeast to 38% in the West (May through July 2026). Among the top 25% of businesses by close rate in each region, medians ranged from 70% to 73%. The page does not define close rate and says the data should not be read as representative of the entire trades industry.

Work out your close rate:
1. Count the estimates you gave this month.
2. Count the jobs you sold this month.
3. Close rate = jobs sold / estimates given. Example: 40 estimates, 14 sold. 14 / 40 = 35%.
4. Every Friday, write both numbers down. Then run it in dollars: $ sold / $ quoted. If the dollar rate is lower, your bigger quotes are the ones getting away.
5. The first number to beat is your own, from last month.

Send this to whoever writes your estimates.
